### HttpAuthMiddleware

***class*scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.httpauth.HttpAuthMiddleware[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/httpauth.html#HttpAuthMiddleware)**

This middleware authenticates all requests generated from certain spiders
using [Basic access authentication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication) (aka. HTTP auth).

To enable HTTP authentication for a spider, set the `http_user` and
`http_pass` spider attributes to the authentication data and the
`http_auth_domain` spider attribute to the domain which requires this
authentication (its subdomains will be also handled in the same way).
You can set `http_auth_domain` to `None` to enable the
authentication for all requests but you risk leaking your authentication
credentials to unrelated domains.

In previous Scrapy versions HttpAuthMiddleware sent the authentication
data with all requests, which is a security problem if the spider
makes requests to several different domains. Currently if the
`http_auth_domain` attribute is not set, the middleware will use the
domain of the first request, which will work for some spiders but not
for others. In the future the middleware will produce an error instead.

Example:

```
from scrapy.spiders import CrawlSpider

class SomeIntranetSiteSpider(CrawlSpider):
    http_user = "someuser"
    http_pass = "somepass"
    http_auth_domain = "intranet.example.com"
    name = "intranet.example.com"

    # .. rest of the spider code omitted ...
```

### HttpCacheMiddleware

***class*scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.httpcache.HttpCacheMiddleware[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/httpcache.html#HttpCacheMiddleware)**

This middleware provides low-level cache to all HTTP requests and responses.
It has to be combined with a cache storage backend as well as a cache policy.

Scrapy ships with the following HTTP cache storage backends:

> - Filesystem storage backend (default)
> - DBM storage backend

You can change the HTTP cache storage backend with the `HTTPCACHE_STORAGE`
setting. Or you can also implement your own storage backend.

Scrapy ships with two HTTP cache policies:

> - RFC2616 policy
> - Dummy policy (default)

You can change the HTTP cache policy with the `HTTPCACHE_POLICY`
setting. Or you can also implement your own policy.

You can also avoid caching a response on every policy using `dont_cache` meta key equals `True`.

#### Dummy policy (default)

***class*scrapy.extensions.httpcache.DummyPolicy[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/extensions/httpcache.html#DummyPolicy)**

This policy has no awareness of any HTTP Cache-Control directives.
Every request and its corresponding response are cached. When the same
request is seen again, the response is returned without transferring
anything from the Internet.

The Dummy policy is useful for testing spiders faster (without having
to wait for downloads every time) and for trying your spider offline,
when an Internet connection is not available. The goal is to be able to
“replay” a spider run *exactly as it ran before*.

#### RFC2616 policy

***class*scrapy.extensions.httpcache.RFC2616Policy[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/extensions/httpcache.html#RFC2616Policy)**

This policy provides a RFC2616 compliant HTTP cache, i.e. with HTTP
Cache-Control awareness, aimed at production and used in continuous
runs to avoid downloading unmodified data (to save bandwidth and speed up
crawls).

What is implemented:

- Do not attempt to store responses/requests with `no-store` cache-control directive set
- Do not serve responses from cache if `no-cache` cache-control directive is set even for fresh responses
- Compute freshness lifetime from `max-age` cache-control directive
- Compute freshness lifetime from `Expires` response header
- Compute freshness lifetime from `Last-Modified` response header (heuristic used by Firefox)
- Compute current age from `Age` response header
- Compute current age from `Date` header
- Revalidate stale responses based on `Last-Modified` response header
- Revalidate stale responses based on `ETag` response header
- Set `Date` header for any received response missing it
- Support `max-stale` cache-control directive in requests

This allows spiders to be configured with the full RFC2616 cache policy,
but avoid revalidation on a request-by-request basis, while remaining
conformant with the HTTP spec.

Example:

Add `Cache-Control: max-stale=600` to Request headers to accept responses that
have exceeded their expiration time by no more than 600 seconds.

See also: RFC2616, 14.9.3

What is missing:

- `Pragma: no-cache` support [https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec14.html#sec14.9.1](https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec14.html#sec14.9.1)
- `Vary` header support [https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec13.html#sec13.6](https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec13.html#sec13.6)
- Invalidation after updates or deletes [https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec13.html#sec13.10](https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec13.html#sec13.10)
- … probably others ..

#### Filesystem storage backend (default)

***class*scrapy.extensions.httpcache.FilesystemCacheStorage[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/extensions/httpcache.html#FilesystemCacheStorage)**

File system storage backend is available for the HTTP cache middleware.

Each request/response pair is stored in a different directory containing
the following files:

- `request_body` - the plain request body
- `request_headers` - the request headers (in raw HTTP format)
- `response_body` - the plain response body
- `response_headers` - the request headers (in raw HTTP format)
- `meta` - some metadata of this cache resource in Python `repr()`
format (grep-friendly format)
- `pickled_meta` - the same metadata in `meta` but pickled for more
efficient deserialization

The directory name is made from the request fingerprint (see
`scrapy.utils.request.fingerprint`), and one level of subdirectories is
used to avoid creating too many files into the same directory (which is
inefficient in many file systems). An example directory could be:

```
/path/to/cache/dir/example.com/72/72811f648e718090f041317756c03adb0ada46c7
```

#### DBM storage backend

***class*scrapy.extensions.httpcache.DbmCacheStorage[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/extensions/httpcache.html#DbmCacheStorage)**

A [DBM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dbm) storage backend is also available for the HTTP cache middleware.

By default, it uses the [`dbm`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/dbm.html#module-dbm), but you can change it with the
`HTTPCACHE_DBM_MODULE` setting.

#### Writing your own storage backend

You can implement a cache storage backend by creating a Python class that
defines the methods described below.

***class*scrapy.extensions.httpcache.CacheStorage**

**open_spider(*spider*)**

This method gets called after a spider has been opened for crawling. It handles
the [`open_spider`](signals.html#std-signal-spider_opened) signal.

**Parameters:**

**spider** ([`Spider`](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider) object) – the spider which has been opened

**close_spider(*spider*)**

This method gets called after a spider has been closed. It handles
the [`close_spider`](signals.html#std-signal-spider_closed) signal.

**Parameters:**

**spider** ([`Spider`](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider) object) – the spider which has been closed

**retrieve_response(*spider*, *request*)**

Return response if present in cache, or `None` otherwise.

**Parameters:**

- **spider** ([`Spider`](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider) object) – the spider which generated the request
- **request** ([`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object) – the request to find cached response for

**store_response(*spider*, *request*, *response*)**

Store the given response in the cache.

**Parameters:**

- **spider** ([`Spider`](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider) object) – the spider for which the response is intended
- **request** ([`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object) – the corresponding request the spider generated
- **response** ([`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object) – the response to store in the cache

In order to use your storage backend, set:

- `HTTPCACHE_STORAGE` to the Python import path of your custom storage class.

#### HTTPCache middleware settings

The `HttpCacheMiddleware` can be configured through the following
settings:

##### HTTPCACHE_ENABLED

Default: `False`

Whether the HTTP cache will be enabled.

##### HTTPCACHE_EXPIRATION_SECS

Default: `0`

Expiration time for cached requests, in seconds.

Cached requests older than this time will be re-downloaded. If zero, cached
requests will never expire.

##### HTTPCACHE_DIR

Default: `'httpcache'`

The directory to use for storing the (low-level) HTTP cache. If empty, the HTTP
cache will be disabled. If a relative path is given, is taken relative to the
project data dir. For more info see: [Default structure of Scrapy projects](commands.html#topics-project-structure).

##### HTTPCACHE_IGNORE_HTTP_CODES

Default: `[]`

Don’t cache response with these HTTP codes.

##### HTTPCACHE_IGNORE_MISSING

Default: `False`

If enabled, requests not found in the cache will be ignored instead of downloaded.

##### HTTPCACHE_IGNORE_SCHEMES

Default: `['file']`

Don’t cache responses with these URI schemes.

##### HTTPCACHE_STORAGE

Default: `'scrapy.extensions.httpcache.FilesystemCacheStorage'`

The class which implements the cache storage backend.

##### HTTPCACHE_DBM_MODULE

Default: `'dbm'`

The database module to use in the DBM storage backend. This setting is specific to the DBM backend.

##### HTTPCACHE_POLICY

Default: `'scrapy.extensions.httpcache.DummyPolicy'`

The class which implements the cache policy.

##### HTTPCACHE_GZIP

Default: `False`

If enabled, will compress all cached data with gzip.
This setting is specific to the Filesystem backend.

##### HTTPCACHE_ALWAYS_STORE

Default: `False`

If enabled, will cache pages unconditionally.

A spider may wish to have all responses available in the cache, for
future use with `Cache-Control: max-stale`, for instance. The
DummyPolicy caches all responses but never revalidates them, and
sometimes a more nuanced policy is desirable.

This setting still respects `Cache-Control: no-store` directives in responses.
If you don’t want that, filter `no-store` out of the Cache-Control headers in
responses you feed to the cache middleware.

##### HTTPCACHE_IGNORE_RESPONSE_CACHE_CONTROLS

Default: `[]`

List of Cache-Control directives in responses to be ignored.

Sites often set “no-store”, “no-cache”, “must-revalidate”, etc., but get
upset at the traffic a spider can generate if it actually respects those
directives. This allows to selectively ignore Cache-Control directives
that are known to be unimportant for the sites being crawled.

We assume that the spider will not issue Cache-Control directives
in requests unless it actually needs them, so directives in requests are
not filtered.

### HttpCompressionMiddleware

***class*scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.httpcompression.HttpCompressionMiddleware[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/httpcompression.html#HttpCompressionMiddleware)**

### HttpProxyMiddleware

***class*scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.httpproxy.HttpProxyMiddleware[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/httpproxy.html#HttpProxyMiddleware)**

This middleware sets the HTTP proxy to use for requests, by setting the

Like the Python standard library module [`urllib.request`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/urllib.request.html#module-urllib.request), it obeys
the following environment variables:

- `http_proxy`
- `https_proxy`
- `no_proxy`

You can also set the meta key `proxy` per-request, to a value like

Keep in mind this value will take precedence over `http_proxy`/`https_proxy`
environment variables, and it will also ignore `no_proxy` environment variable.

### OffsiteMiddleware

***class*scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.offsite.OffsiteMiddleware[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/offsite.html#OffsiteMiddleware)**

Added in version 2.11.2.

Filters out Requests for URLs outside the domains covered by the spider.

This middleware filters out every request whose host names aren’t in the
spider’s [`allowed_domains`](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider.allowed_domains) attribute.
All subdomains of any domain in the list are also allowed.
E.g. the rule `www.example.org` will also allow `bob.www.example.org`
but not `www2.example.com` nor `example.com`.

When your spider returns a request for a domain not belonging to those
covered by the spider, this middleware will log a debug message similar to
this one:

```
DEBUG: Filtered offsite request to 'offsite.example': <GET http://offsite.example/some/page.html>
```

To avoid filling the log with too much noise, it will only print one of
these messages for each new domain filtered. So, for example, if another
request for `offsite.example` is filtered, no log message will be
printed. But if a request for `other.example` is filtered, a message
will be printed (but only for the first request filtered).

If the spider doesn’t define an
[`allowed_domains`](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider.allowed_domains) attribute, or the
attribute is empty, the offsite middleware will allow all requests.

If the request has the [`dont_filter`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request.dont_filter) attribute set to
`True` or `Request.meta` has `allow_offsite` set to `True`, then
the OffsiteMiddleware will allow the request even if its domain is not listed
in allowed domains.

### RedirectMiddleware

***class*scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.redirect.RedirectMiddleware[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/redirect.html#RedirectMiddleware)**

This middleware handles redirection of requests based on response status.

The urls which the request goes through (while being redirected) can be found
in the `redirect_urls` [`Request.meta`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request.meta) key.

The reason behind each redirect in `redirect_urls` can be found in the
`redirect_reasons` [`Request.meta`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request.meta) key. For
example: `[301, 302, 307, 'meta refresh']`.

The format of a reason depends on the middleware that handled the corresponding
redirect. For example, `RedirectMiddleware` indicates the triggering
response status code as an integer, while `MetaRefreshMiddleware`
always uses the `'meta refresh'` string as reason.

The `RedirectMiddleware` can be configured through the following
settings (see the settings documentation for more info):

- `REDIRECT_ENABLED`
- `REDIRECT_MAX_TIMES`

If [`Request.meta`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request.meta) has `dont_redirect`
key set to True, the request will be ignored by this middleware.

If you want to handle some redirect status codes in your spider, you can
specify these in the `handle_httpstatus_list` spider attribute.

For example, if you want the redirect middleware to ignore 301 and 302
responses (and pass them through to your spider) you can do this:

```
class MySpider(CrawlSpider):
    handle_httpstatus_list = [301, 302]
```

The `handle_httpstatus_list` key of [`Request.meta`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request.meta) can also be used to specify which response codes to
allow on a per-request basis. You can also set the meta key
`handle_httpstatus_all` to `True` if you want to allow any response code
for a request.

#### RedirectMiddleware settings

##### REDIRECT_ENABLED

Default: `True`

Whether the Redirect middleware will be enabled.

##### REDIRECT_MAX_TIMES

Default: `20`

The maximum number of redirections that will be followed for a single request.
If maximum redirections are exceeded, the request is aborted and ignored.

### MetaRefreshMiddleware

***class*scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.redirect.MetaRefreshMiddleware[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/redirect.html#MetaRefreshMiddleware)**

This middleware handles redirection of requests based on meta-refresh html tag.

The `MetaRefreshMiddleware` can be configured through the following
settings (see the settings documentation for more info):

- `METAREFRESH_ENABLED`
- `METAREFRESH_IGNORE_TAGS`
- `METAREFRESH_MAXDELAY`

This middleware obey `REDIRECT_MAX_TIMES` setting, `dont_redirect`,
`redirect_urls` and `redirect_reasons` request meta keys as described
for `RedirectMiddleware`

#### MetaRefreshMiddleware settings

##### METAREFRESH_ENABLED

Default: `True`

Whether the Meta Refresh middleware will be enabled.

##### METAREFRESH_IGNORE_TAGS

Default: `[]`

Meta tags within these tags are ignored.

Changed in version 2.11.2: The default value of `METAREFRESH_IGNORE_TAGS` changed from
`[]` to `["noscript"]`.

##### METAREFRESH_MAXDELAY

Default: `100`

The maximum meta-refresh delay (in seconds) to follow the redirection.
Some sites use meta-refresh for redirecting to a session expired page, so we
restrict automatic redirection to the maximum delay.

### RetryMiddleware

***class*scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.retry.RetryMiddleware[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/retry.html#RetryMiddleware)**

A middleware to retry failed requests that are potentially caused by
temporary problems such as a connection timeout or HTTP 500 error.

Failed pages are collected on the scraping process and rescheduled at the
end, once the spider has finished crawling all regular (non failed) pages.

The `RetryMiddleware` can be configured through the following
settings (see the settings documentation for more info):

- `RETRY_ENABLED`
- `RETRY_TIMES`
- `RETRY_HTTP_CODES`
- `RETRY_EXCEPTIONS`

If [`Request.meta`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request.meta) has `dont_retry` key
set to True, the request will be ignored by this middleware.

To retry requests from a spider callback, you can use the
`get_retry_request()` function:

**scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.retry.get_retry_request(*request: Request*, ***, *spider: Spider*, *reason: str | Exception | type[Exception] = 'unspecified'*, *max_retry_times: int | None = None*, *priority_adjust: int | None = None*, *logger: Logger = <Logger scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.retry (WARNING)>*, *stats_base_key: str = 'retry'*) → [Request](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/library/constants.html#None)[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/retry.html#get_retry_request)**

Returns a new [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object to retry the specified
request, or `None` if retries of the specified request have been
exhausted.

For example, in a [`Spider`](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider) callback, you could use it as
follows:

```
def parse(self, response):
    if not response.text:
        new_request_or_none = get_retry_request(
            response.request,
            spider=self,
            reason='empty',
        )
        return new_request_or_none
```

*spider* is the [`Spider`](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider) instance which is asking for the
retry request. It is used to access the [settings](settings.html#topics-settings)
and [stats](stats.html#topics-stats), and to provide extra logging context (see
[`logging.debug()`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logging.debug)).

*reason* is a string or an [`Exception`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#Exception) object that indicates the
reason why the request needs to be retried. It is used to name retry stats.

*max_retry_times* is a number that determines the maximum number of times
that *request* can be retried. If not specified or `None`, the number is
read from the [`max_retry_times`](request-response.html#std-reqmeta-max_retry_times) meta key of the request. If the
[`max_retry_times`](request-response.html#std-reqmeta-max_retry_times) meta key is not defined or `None`, the number
is read from the `RETRY_TIMES` setting.

*priority_adjust* is a number that determines how the priority of the new
request changes in relation to *request*. If not specified, the number is
read from the `RETRY_PRIORITY_ADJUST` setting.

*logger* is the logging.Logger object to be used when logging messages

*stats_base_key* is a string to be used as the base key for the
retry-related job stats

#### RetryMiddleware Settings

##### RETRY_ENABLED

Default: `True`

Whether the Retry middleware will be enabled.

##### RETRY_TIMES

Default: `2`

Maximum number of times to retry, in addition to the first download.

Maximum number of retries can also be specified per-request using
[`max_retry_times`](request-response.html#std-reqmeta-max_retry_times) attribute of [`Request.meta`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request.meta).
When initialized, the [`max_retry_times`](request-response.html#std-reqmeta-max_retry_times) meta key takes higher
precedence over the `RETRY_TIMES` setting.

##### RETRY_HTTP_CODES

Default: `[500, 502, 503, 504, 522, 524, 408, 429]`

Which HTTP response codes to retry. Other errors (DNS lookup issues,
connections lost, etc) are always retried.

In some cases you may want to add 400 to `RETRY_HTTP_CODES` because
it is a common code used to indicate server overload. It is not included by
default because HTTP specs say so.

##### RETRY_EXCEPTIONS

Default:

```
[
    'twisted.internet.defer.TimeoutError',
    'twisted.internet.error.TimeoutError',
    'twisted.internet.error.DNSLookupError',
    'twisted.internet.error.ConnectionRefusedError',
    'twisted.internet.error.ConnectionDone',
    'twisted.internet.error.ConnectError',
    'twisted.internet.error.ConnectionLost',
    'twisted.internet.error.TCPTimedOutError',
    'twisted.web.client.ResponseFailed',
    IOError,
    'scrapy.core.downloader.handlers.http11.TunnelError',
]
```

List of exceptions to retry.

Each list entry may be an exception type or its import path as a string.

An exception will not be caught when the exception type is not in
`RETRY_EXCEPTIONS` or when the maximum number of retries for a request
has been exceeded (see `RETRY_TIMES`). To learn about uncaught
exception propagation, see
`process_exception()`.

##### RETRY_PRIORITY_ADJUST

Default: `-1`

Adjust retry request priority relative to original request:

- a positive priority adjust means higher priority.
- **a negative priority adjust (default) means lower priority.**

### RobotsTxtMiddleware

***class*scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.robotstxt.RobotsTxtMiddleware[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/robotstxt.html#RobotsTxtMiddleware)**

This middleware filters out requests forbidden by the robots.txt exclusion
standard.

To make sure Scrapy respects robots.txt make sure the middleware is enabled
and the [`ROBOTSTXT_OBEY`](settings.html#std-setting-ROBOTSTXT_OBEY) setting is enabled.

The [`ROBOTSTXT_USER_AGENT`](settings.html#std-setting-ROBOTSTXT_USER_AGENT) setting can be used to specify the
user agent string to use for matching in the [robots.txt](https://www.robotstxt.org/) file. If it
is `None`, the User-Agent header you are sending with the request or the
[`USER_AGENT`](settings.html#std-setting-USER_AGENT) setting (in that order) will be used for determining
the user agent to use in the [robots.txt](https://www.robotstxt.org/) file.

This middleware has to be combined with a [robots.txt](https://www.robotstxt.org/) parser.

Scrapy ships with support for the following [robots.txt](https://www.robotstxt.org/) parsers:

- Protego (default)
- RobotFileParser
- Robotexclusionrulesparser

You can change the [robots.txt](https://www.robotstxt.org/) parser with the [`ROBOTSTXT_PARSER`](settings.html#std-setting-ROBOTSTXT_PARSER)
setting. Or you can also implement support for a new parser.

If [`Request.meta`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request.meta) has
`dont_obey_robotstxt` key set to True
the request will be ignored by this middleware even if
[`ROBOTSTXT_OBEY`](settings.html#std-setting-ROBOTSTXT_OBEY) is enabled.

Parsers vary in several aspects:

- Language of implementation
- Supported specification
- Support for wildcard matching
- Usage of [length based rule](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/robots_txt#order-of-precedence-for-rules):
in particular for `Allow` and `Disallow` directives, where the most
specific rule based on the length of the path trumps the less specific
(shorter) rule

Performance comparison of different parsers is available at [the following link](https://github.com/scrapy/scrapy/issues/3969).

#### Protego parser

Based on [Protego](https://github.com/scrapy/protego):

- implemented in Python
- is compliant with [Google’s Robots.txt Specification](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/robots_txt)
- supports wildcard matching
- uses the length based rule

Scrapy uses this parser by default.

#### RobotFileParser

Based on [`RobotFileParser`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/urllib.robotparser.html#urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser):

- is Python’s built-in [robots.txt](https://www.robotstxt.org/) parser
- is compliant with [Martijn Koster’s 1996 draft specification](https://www.robotstxt.org/norobots-rfc.txt)
- lacks support for wildcard matching
- doesn’t use the length based rule

It is faster than Protego and backward-compatible with versions of Scrapy before 1.8.0.

In order to use this parser, set:

- [`ROBOTSTXT_PARSER`](settings.html#std-setting-ROBOTSTXT_PARSER) to `scrapy.robotstxt.PythonRobotParser`

#### Robotexclusionrulesparser

Based on [Robotexclusionrulesparser](https://pypi.org/project/robotexclusionrulesparser/):

- implemented in Python
- is compliant with [Martijn Koster’s 1996 draft specification](https://www.robotstxt.org/norobots-rfc.txt)
- supports wildcard matching
- doesn’t use the length based rule

In order to use this parser:

- Install `Robotexclusionrulesparser` by running
`pip install robotexclusionrulesparser`
- Set [`ROBOTSTXT_PARSER`](settings.html#std-setting-ROBOTSTXT_PARSER) setting to
`scrapy.robotstxt.RerpRobotParser`

#### Implementing support for a new parser

You can implement support for a new [robots.txt](https://www.robotstxt.org/) parser by subclassing
the abstract base class `RobotParser` and
implementing the methods described below.

***class*scrapy.robotstxt.RobotParser[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/robotstxt.html#RobotParser)**

***abstract*allowed(*url: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str) | [bytes](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes)*, *user_agent: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str) | [bytes](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes)*) → [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool)[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/robotstxt.html#RobotParser.allowed)**

Return `True` if `user_agent` is allowed to crawl `url`, otherwise return `False`.

**Parameters:**

- **url** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*bytes*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes)) – Absolute URL
- **user_agent** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str)*or*[*bytes*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes)) – User agent

***abstract classmethod*from_crawler(*crawler: [Crawler](api.html#scrapy.crawler.Crawler)*, *robotstxt_body: [bytes](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes)*) → Self[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/robotstxt.html#RobotParser.from_crawler)**

Parse the content of a [robots.txt](https://www.robotstxt.org/) file as bytes. This must be a class method.
It must return a new instance of the parser backend.

**Parameters:**

- **crawler** ([`Crawler`](api.html#scrapy.crawler.Crawler) instance) – crawler which made the request
- **robotstxt_body** ([*bytes*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes)) – content of a [robots.txt](https://www.robotstxt.org/) file.

### DownloaderStats

***class*scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.stats.DownloaderStats[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/stats.html#DownloaderStats)**

Middleware that stores stats of all requests, responses and exceptions that
pass through it.

To use this middleware you must enable the [`DOWNLOADER_STATS`](settings.html#std-setting-DOWNLOADER_STATS)
setting.

### UserAgentMiddleware

***class*scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.useragent.UserAgentMiddleware[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/useragent.html#UserAgentMiddleware)**

Middleware that sets the `User-Agent` header.

The header value is taken from the [`USER_AGENT`](settings.html#std-setting-USER_AGENT) setting.

sections.heading: Downloader Middleware
sections.text:
The downloader middleware is a framework of hooks into Scrapy’s
request/response processing. It’s a light, low-level system for globally
altering Scrapy’s requests and responses.

metadata.section_summary: The downloader middleware is a framework of hooks into Scrapy’s

sections.heading: Activating a downloader middleware
sections.text:
To activate a downloader middleware component, add it to the
[`DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES`](settings.html#std-setting-DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES) setting, which is a dict whose keys are the
middleware class paths and their values are the middleware orders.

Here’s an example:

```
DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES = {
    "myproject.middlewares.CustomDownloaderMiddleware": 543,
}
```

The [`DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES`](settings.html#std-setting-DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES) setting is merged with the
[`DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES_BASE`](settings.html#std-setting-DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES_BASE) setting defined in Scrapy (and not meant
to be overridden) and then sorted by order to get the final sorted list of
enabled middlewares: the first middleware is the one closer to the engine and
the last is the one closer to the downloader. In other words,
the `process_request()`
method of each middleware will be invoked in increasing
middleware order (100, 200, 300, …) and the `process_response()` method
of each middleware will be invoked in decreasing order.

To decide which order to assign to your middleware see the
[`DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES_BASE`](settings.html#std-setting-DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES_BASE) setting and pick a value according to
where you want to insert the middleware. The order does matter because each
middleware performs a different action and your middleware could depend on some
previous (or subsequent) middleware being applied.

If you want to disable a built-in middleware (the ones defined in
[`DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES_BASE`](settings.html#std-setting-DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES_BASE) and enabled by default) you must define it
in your project’s [`DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES`](settings.html#std-setting-DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES) setting and assign `None`
as its value. For example, if you want to disable the user-agent middleware:

```
DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES = {
    "myproject.middlewares.CustomDownloaderMiddleware": 543,
    "scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.useragent.UserAgentMiddleware": None,
}
```

Finally, keep in mind that some middlewares may need to be enabled through a
particular setting. See each middleware documentation for more info.

sections.heading: Writing your own downloader middleware
sections.text:
Each downloader middleware is a [component](components.html#topics-components) that
defines one or more of these methods:

***class*scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.DownloaderMiddleware**

Any of the downloader middleware methods may be defined as a
coroutine function (`async def`).

**process_request(*request*)**

This method is called for each request that goes through the download
middleware.

`process_request()` should either: return `None`, return a
[`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object, return a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request)
object, or raise [`IgnoreRequest`](exceptions.html#scrapy.exceptions.IgnoreRequest).

If it returns `None`, Scrapy will continue processing this request, executing all
other middlewares until, finally, the appropriate downloader handler is called
the request performed (and its response downloaded).

If it returns a [`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object, Scrapy won’t bother
calling *any* other `process_request()` or `process_exception()` methods,
or the appropriate download function; it’ll return that response. The `process_response()`
methods of installed middleware is always called on every response.

If it returns a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object, Scrapy will stop calling
`process_request()` methods and reschedule the returned request. Once the newly returned
request is performed, the appropriate middleware chain will be called on
the downloaded response.

If it raises an [`IgnoreRequest`](exceptions.html#scrapy.exceptions.IgnoreRequest) exception, the
`process_exception()` methods of installed downloader middleware will be called.
If none of them handle the exception, the errback function of the request
(`Request.errback`) is called. If no code handles the raised exception, it is
ignored and not logged (unlike other exceptions).

**Parameters:**

**request** ([`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object) – the request being processed

**process_response(*request*, *response*)**

`process_response()` should either: return a [`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response)
object, return a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object or
raise a [`IgnoreRequest`](exceptions.html#scrapy.exceptions.IgnoreRequest) exception.

If it returns a [`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) (it could be the same given
response, or a brand-new one), that response will continue to be processed
with the `process_response()` of the next middleware in the chain.

If it returns a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object, the middleware chain is
halted and the returned request is rescheduled to be downloaded in the future.
This is the same behavior as if a request is returned from `process_request()`.

If it raises an [`IgnoreRequest`](exceptions.html#scrapy.exceptions.IgnoreRequest) exception, the errback
function of the request (`Request.errback`) is called. If no code handles the raised
exception, it is ignored and not logged (unlike other exceptions).

**Parameters:**

- **request** (is a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object) – the request that originated the response
- **response** ([`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object) – the response being processed

**process_exception(*request*, *exception*)**

Scrapy calls `process_exception()` when a [download handler](download-handlers.html#topics-download-handlers) or a `process_request()` (from a
downloader middleware) raises an exception (including an
[`IgnoreRequest`](exceptions.html#scrapy.exceptions.IgnoreRequest) exception).

`process_exception()` should return: either `None`,
a [`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object, or a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object.

If it returns `None`, Scrapy will continue processing this exception,
executing any other `process_exception()` methods of installed middleware,
until no middleware is left and the default exception handling kicks in.

If it returns a [`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object, the `process_response()`
method chain of installed middleware is started, and Scrapy won’t bother calling
any other `process_exception()` methods of middleware.

If it returns a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object, the returned request is
rescheduled to be downloaded in the future. This stops the execution of
`process_exception()` methods of the middleware the same as returning a
response would.

**Parameters:**

- **request** (is a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object) – the request that generated the exception
- **exception** (an `Exception` object) – the raised exception

The spider middleware is a framework of hooks into Scrapy’s spider processing
mechanism where you can plug custom functionality to process the responses that
are sent to [Spiders](spiders.html#topics-spiders) for processing and to process the requests
and items that are generated from spiders.

Activating a spider middleware
To activate a spider middleware component, add it to the
[`SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES`](settings.html#std-setting-SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES) setting, which is a dict whose keys are the
middleware class path and their values are the middleware orders.

Here’s an example:

```
SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES = {
    "myproject.middlewares.CustomSpiderMiddleware": 543,
}
```

```
SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES = {
    "scrapy.spidermiddlewares.referer.RefererMiddleware": None,
    "myproject.middlewares.CustomRefererSpiderMiddleware": 700,
}
```

Finally, keep in mind that some middlewares may need to be enabled through a
particular setting. See each middleware documentation for more info.

Writing your own spider middleware
Each spider middleware is a [component](components.html#topics-components) that defines
one or more of these methods:

***class*scrapy.spidermiddlewares.SpiderMiddleware**

***async*process_start(*start: AsyncIterator[Any]*, */*) → AsyncIterator[Any]**

Iterate over the output of [`start()`](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider.start) or that
of the `process_start()` method of an earlier spider middleware,
overriding it. For example:

```
async def process_start(self, start):
    async for item_or_request in start:
        yield item_or_request
```

You may yield the same type of objects as [`start()`](spiders.html#scrapy.Spider.start).

To write spider middlewares that work on Scrapy versions lower than
2.13, define also a synchronous `process_start_requests()` method
that returns an iterable. For example:

```
def process_start_requests(self, start, spider):
    yield from start
```

**process_spider_input(*response*)**

This method is called for each response that goes through the spider
middleware and into the spider, for processing.

`process_spider_input()` should return `None` or raise an
exception.

If it returns `None`, Scrapy will continue processing this response,
executing all other middlewares until, finally, the response is handed
to the spider for processing.

**Parameters:**

If defined, this method must be an [asynchronous generator](https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-generator),
which will be called instead of `process_spider_output()` if
`result` is an [asynchronous iterable](https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterable).

**process_spider_exception(*response*, *exception*)**

This method is called when a spider or `process_spider_output()`
method (from a previous spider middleware) raises an exception.

`process_spider_exception()` should return either `None` or an
iterable of [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) or [item](items.html#topics-items)
objects.

If it returns `None`, Scrapy will continue processing this exception,
executing any other `process_spider_exception()` in the following
middleware components, until no middleware components are left and the
exception reaches the engine (where it’s logged and discarded).

If it returns an iterable the `process_spider_output()` pipeline
kicks in, starting from the next spider middleware, and no other
`process_spider_exception()` will be called.

**Parameters:**

- **response** ([`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object) – the response being processed when the exception was
raised
- **exception** ([`Exception`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#Exception) object) – the exception raised

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
import warnings
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from scrapy import Request, Spider, signals
from scrapy.exceptions import IgnoreRequest
from scrapy.utils.decorators import _warn_spider_arg
from scrapy.utils.httpobj import urlparse_cached

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    # typing.Self requires Python 3.11
    from typing_extensions import Self

from scrapy.crawler import Crawler
    from scrapy.statscollectors import StatsCollector

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

[docs]
class OffsiteMiddleware:
    crawler: Crawler

def __init__(self, stats: StatsCollector):
        self.stats = stats
        self.domains_seen: set[str] = set()

def spider_opened(self, spider: Spider) -> None:
        self.host_regex: re.Pattern[str] = self.get_host_regex(spider)

def request_scheduled(self, request: Request, spider: Spider) -> None:
        self.process_request(request)

def should_follow(self, request: Request, spider: Spider) -> bool:
        regex = self.host_regex
        # hostname can be None for wrong urls (like javascript links)
        host = urlparse_cached(request).hostname or ""
        return bool(regex.search(host))

Create a Request object from a string containing a [cURL](https://curl.se/) command. It populates the HTTP method, the
URL, the headers, the cookies and the body. It accepts the same
arguments as the `Request` class, taking preference and
overriding the values of the same arguments contained in the cURL
command.

Unrecognized options are ignored by default. To raise an error when
finding unknown options call this method by passing
`ignore_unknown_options=False`.

To translate a cURL command into a Scrapy request,
you may use [curl2scrapy](https://michael-shub.github.io/curl2scrapy/).

Return a dictionary containing the Request’s data.

Use `request_from_dict()` to convert back into a `Request` object.

If a spider is given, this method will try to find out the name of the spider methods used as callback
and errback and include them in the output dict, raising an exception if they cannot be found.

When assigned to the `callback` parameter of
`Request`, it indicates that the request is not meant
to have a spider callback at all.

For example:

```
Request("https://example.com", callback=NO_CALLBACK)
```

Create a `Request` object from a dict.

If a spider is given, it will try to resolve the callbacks looking at the
spider for methods with the same name.

Passing additional data to callback functions
The callback of a request is a function that will be called when the response
of that request is downloaded. The callback function will be called with the
downloaded `Response` object as its first argument.

Example:

```
def parse_page1(self, response):
    return scrapy.Request(
        "http://www.example.com/some_page.html", callback=self.parse_page2
    )

def parse_page2(self, response):
    # this would log http://www.example.com/some_page.html
    self.logger.info("Visited %s", response.url)
```

In some cases you may be interested in passing arguments to those callback
functions so you can receive the arguments later, in the second callback.
The following example shows how to achieve this by using the

async def start(self):
        for u in self.start_urls:
            yield scrapy.Request(
                u,
                callback=self.parse_httpbin,
                errback=self.errback_httpbin,
                dont_filter=True,
            )

def parse_httpbin(self, response):
        self.logger.info("Got successful response from {}".format(response.url))
        # do something useful here...

def errback_httpbin(self, failure):
        # log all failures
        self.logger.error(repr(failure))

# in case you want to do something special for some errors,
        # you may need the failure's type:

if failure.check(HttpError):
            # these exceptions come from HttpError spider middleware
            # you can get the non-200 response
            response = failure.value.response
            self.logger.error("HttpError on %s", response.url)

elif failure.check(DNSLookupError):
            # this is the original request
            request = failure.request
            self.logger.error("DNSLookupError on %s", request.url)

elif failure.check(TimeoutError, TCPTimedOutError):
            request = failure.request
            self.logger.error("TimeoutError on %s", request.url)
```

achieve this by using `Failure.request.cb_kwargs`:

        "http://www.example.com/index.html",
        callback=self.parse_page2,
        errback=self.errback_page2,
        cb_kwargs=dict(main_url=response.url),
    )
    yield request

def parse_page2(self, response, main_url):
    pass

def errback_page2(self, failure):
    yield dict(
        main_url=failure.request.cb_kwargs["main_url"],
    )
```

To change how request fingerprints are built for your requests, use the
`REQUEST_FINGERPRINTER_CLASS` setting.

REQUEST_FINGERPRINTER_CLASS
Default: `scrapy.utils.request.RequestFingerprinter`

A request fingerprinter class or its
import path.

***class*scrapy.utils.request.RequestFingerprinter(*crawler: [Crawler](api.html#scrapy.crawler.Crawler) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/library/constants.html#None) = None*)[[source]](../_modules/scrapy/utils/request.html#RequestFingerprinter)**

Default fingerprinter.

It takes into account a canonical version
([`w3lib.url.canonicalize_url()`](https://w3lib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/w3lib.html#w3lib.url.canonicalize_url)) of `request.url` and the values of `request.method` and `request.body`. It then generates an [SHA1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-1) hash.

Writing your own request fingerprinter
A request fingerprinter is a [component](components.html#topics-components) that must
implement the following method:

**fingerprint(*self*, *request: scrapy.Request*)**

Return a [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes) object that uniquely identifies *request*.

See also Request fingerprint restrictions.

The `fingerprint()` method of the default request fingerprinter,
`scrapy.utils.request.RequestFingerprinter`, uses
`scrapy.utils.request.fingerprint()` with its default parameters. For some
common use cases you can use `scrapy.utils.request.fingerprint()` as well
in your `fingerprint()` method implementation:

Return the request fingerprint.

The request fingerprint is a hash that uniquely identifies the resource the
request points to. For example, take the following two urls:
`http://www.example.com/query?id=111&cat=222`,
`http://www.example.com/query?cat=222&id=111`.

Even though those are two different URLs both point to the same resource
and are equivalent (i.e. they should return the same response).

Another example are cookies used to store session ids. Suppose the
following page is only accessible to authenticated users:
`http://www.example.com/members/offers.html`.

Lots of sites use a cookie to store the session id, which adds a random
component to the HTTP Request and thus should be ignored when calculating
the fingerprint.

For this reason, request headers are ignored by default when calculating
the fingerprint. If you want to include specific headers use the
include_headers argument, which is a list of Request headers to include.

Also, servers usually ignore fragments in urls when handling requests,
so they are also ignored by default when calculating the fingerprint.
If you want to include them, set the keep_fragments argument to True
(for instance when handling requests with a headless browser).

For example, to take the value of a request header named `X-ID` into
account:

```
# my_project/settings.py
REQUEST_FINGERPRINTER_CLASS = "my_project.utils.RequestFingerprinter"

# my_project/utils.py
from scrapy.utils.request import fingerprint

class RequestFingerprinter:
    def fingerprint(self, request):
        return fingerprint(request, include_headers=["X-ID"])
```

You can also write your own fingerprinting logic from scratch.

However, if you do not use `scrapy.utils.request.fingerprint()`, make sure
you use [`WeakKeyDictionary`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/weakref.html#weakref.WeakKeyDictionary) to cache request fingerprints:

- Caching saves CPU by ensuring that fingerprints are calculated only once
per request, and not once per Scrapy component that needs the fingerprint
of a request.
- Using [`WeakKeyDictionary`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/weakref.html#weakref.WeakKeyDictionary) saves memory by ensuring that
request objects do not stay in memory forever just because you have
references to them in your cache dictionary.

For example, to take into account only the URL of a request, without any prior
URL canonicalization or taking the request method or body into account:

```
from hashlib import sha1
from weakref import WeakKeyDictionary

from scrapy.utils.python import to_bytes

class RequestFingerprinter:
    cache = WeakKeyDictionary()

def fingerprint(self, request):
        if request not in self.cache:
            fp = sha1()
            fp.update(to_bytes(request.url))
            self.cache[request] = fp.digest()
        return self.cache[request]
```

requests from your spider callbacks, you may implement a request fingerprinter
that reads fingerprints from `request.meta`
when available, and then falls back to
`scrapy.utils.request.fingerprint()`. For example:

You can also write your own fingerprinting logic from scratch.

However, if you do not use `scrapy.utils.request.fingerprint()`, make sure
you use [`WeakKeyDictionary`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/weakref.html#weakref.WeakKeyDictionary) to cache request fingerprints:

- Caching saves CPU by ensuring that fingerprints are calculated only once
per request, and not once per Scrapy component that needs the fingerprint
of a request.
- Using [`WeakKeyDictionary`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/weakref.html#weakref.WeakKeyDictionary) saves memory by ensuring that
request objects do not stay in memory forever just because you have
references to them in your cache dictionary.

URL canonicalization or taking the request method or body into account:

```
from hashlib import sha1

    cache = WeakKeyDictionary()

        if request not in self.cache:
            fp = sha1()
            fp.update(to_bytes(request.url))
            self.cache[request] = fp.digest()
        return self.cache[request]
```

requests from your spider callbacks, you may implement a request fingerprinter
that reads fingerprints from `request.meta`
when available, and then falls back to

- **response** (`Response` object) – the response containing a HTML form which will be used
to pre-populate the form fields
- **formname** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str)) – if given, the form with name attribute set to this value will be used.
- **formid** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str)) – if given, the form with id attribute set to this value will be used.
- **formxpath** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str)) – if given, the first form that matches the xpath will be used.
- **formcss** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str)) – if given, the first form that matches the css selector will be used.
- **formnumber** ([*int*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int)) – the number of form to use, when the response contains
multiple forms. The first one (and also the default) is `0`.
- **formdata** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict)) – fields to override in the form data. If a field was
already present in the response `<form>` element, its value is
overridden by the one passed in this parameter. If a value passed in
this parameter is `None`, the field will not be included in the
request, even if it was present in the response `<form>` element.
- **clickdata** ([*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict)) – attributes to lookup the control clicked. If it’s not
given, the form data will be submitted simulating a click on the
first clickable element. In addition to html attributes, the control
can be identified by its zero-based index relative to other
submittable inputs inside the form, via the `nr` attribute.
- **dont_click** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool)) – If True, the form data will be submitted without
clicking in any element.

The other parameters of this class method are passed directly to the
`FormRequest` `__init__()` method.

A string with the encoding of this response. The encoding is resolved by
trying the following mechanisms, in order:

1. the encoding passed in the `__init__()` method `encoding` argument
2. the encoding declared in the Content-Type HTTP header. If this
encoding is not valid (i.e. unknown), it is ignored and the next
resolution mechanism is tried.
3. the encoding declared in the response body. The TextResponse class
doesn’t provide any special functionality for this. However, the
`HtmlResponse` and `XmlResponse` classes do.
4. the encoding inferred by looking at the response body. This is the more
fragile method but also the last one tried.

Return a `Request` instance to follow a link `url`.
It accepts the same arguments as `Request.__init__()` method,
but `url` can be not only an absolute URL, but also

- a relative URL
- a [`Link`](link-extractors.html#scrapy.link.Link) object, e.g. the result of
[Link Extractors](link-extractors.html#topics-link-extractors)
- a [`Selector`](selectors.html#scrapy.Selector) object for a `<link>` or `<a>` element, e.g.
`response.css('a.my_link')[0]`
- an attribute [`Selector`](selectors.html#scrapy.Selector) (not SelectorList), e.g.
`response.css('a::attr(href)')[0]` or
`response.xpath('//img/@src')[0]`

See [A shortcut for creating Requests](../intro/tutorial.html#response-follow-example) for usage examples.

A generator that produces `Request` instances to follow all
links in `urls`. It accepts the same arguments as the `Request`’s
`__init__()` method, except that each `urls` element does not need to be
an absolute URL, it can be any of the following:

- a relative URL
- a [`Link`](link-extractors.html#scrapy.link.Link) object, e.g. the result of
[Link Extractors](link-extractors.html#topics-link-extractors)
- a [`Selector`](selectors.html#scrapy.Selector) object for a `<link>` or `<a>` element, e.g.
`response.css('a.my_link')[0]`
- an attribute [`Selector`](selectors.html#scrapy.Selector) (not SelectorList), e.g.
`response.css('a::attr(href)')[0]` or
`response.xpath('//img/@src')[0]`

In addition, `css` and `xpath` arguments are accepted to perform the link extraction
within the `follow_all()` method (only one of `urls`, `css` and `xpath` is accepted).

Note that when passing a `SelectorList` as argument for the `urls` parameter or
using the `css` or `xpath` parameters, this method will not produce requests for
selectors from which links cannot be obtained (for instance, anchor tags without an
`href` attribute)

support_records.excerpt:
The downloader middleware is a framework of hooks into Scrapy’s
request/response processing. It’s a light, low-level system for globally
altering Scrapy’s requests and responses.

Activating a downloader middleware
To activate a downloader middleware component, add it to the
[`DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES`](settings.html#std-setting-DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES) setting, which is a dict whose keys are the
middleware class paths and their values are the middleware orders.

Here’s an example:

```
DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES = {
    "myproject.middlewares.CustomDownloaderMiddleware": 543,
}
```

```
DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES = {
    "myproject.middlewares.CustomDownloaderMiddleware": 543,
    "scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.useragent.UserAgentMiddleware": None,
}
```

Finally, keep in mind that some middlewares may need to be enabled through a
particular setting. See each middleware documentation for more info.

Writing your own downloader middleware
Each downloader middleware is a [component](components.html#topics-components) that
defines one or more of these methods:

***class*scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.DownloaderMiddleware**

Any of the downloader middleware methods may be defined as a
coroutine function (`async def`).

**process_request(*request*)**

This method is called for each request that goes through the download
middleware.

`process_request()` should either: return `None`, return a
[`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object, return a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request)
object, or raise [`IgnoreRequest`](exceptions.html#scrapy.exceptions.IgnoreRequest).

If it returns `None`, Scrapy will continue processing this request, executing all
other middlewares until, finally, the appropriate downloader handler is called
the request performed (and its response downloaded).

If it returns a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object, Scrapy will stop calling
`process_request()` methods and reschedule the returned request. Once the newly returned
request is performed, the appropriate middleware chain will be called on
the downloaded response.

**Parameters:**

**request** ([`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object) – the request being processed

**process_response(*request*, *response*)**

support_records.excerpt:
`process_response()` should either: return a [`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response)
object, return a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object or
raise a [`IgnoreRequest`](exceptions.html#scrapy.exceptions.IgnoreRequest) exception.

If it returns a [`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) (it could be the same given
response, or a brand-new one), that response will continue to be processed
with the `process_response()` of the next middleware in the chain.

If it returns a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object, the middleware chain is
halted and the returned request is rescheduled to be downloaded in the future.
This is the same behavior as if a request is returned from `process_request()`.

If it raises an [`IgnoreRequest`](exceptions.html#scrapy.exceptions.IgnoreRequest) exception, the errback
function of the request (`Request.errback`) is called. If no code handles the raised
exception, it is ignored and not logged (unlike other exceptions).

**Parameters:**

- **request** (is a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object) – the request that originated the response
- **response** ([`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object) – the response being processed

**process_exception(*request*, *exception*)**

Scrapy calls `process_exception()` when a [download handler](download-handlers.html#topics-download-handlers) or a `process_request()` (from a
downloader middleware) raises an exception (including an
[`IgnoreRequest`](exceptions.html#scrapy.exceptions.IgnoreRequest) exception).

`process_exception()` should return: either `None`,
a [`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object, or a [`Request`](request-response.html#scrapy.Request) object.

If it returns `None`, Scrapy will continue processing this exception,
executing any other `process_exception()` methods of installed middleware,
until no middleware is left and the default exception handling kicks in.

If it returns a [`Response`](request-response.html#scrapy.http.Response) object, the `process_response()`
method chain of installed middleware is started, and Scrapy won’t bother calling
any other `process_exception()` methods of middleware.

skill_specs.name: 启用并排序 Spider 中间件
skill_specs.description: 通过 SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES 设置注册自定义 Spider 中间件并指定执行顺序，可用 None 禁用内置中间件。适用于需要插入或替换 Spider 处理链中某个中间件时。
skill_specs.skill_body:
在 Scrapy 项目的设置中配置 SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES 字典：键为中间件类路径，值为中间件顺序（整数）。如需禁用内置中间件，将其值设为 None。如需替换内置中间件，先禁用原中间件再以新类路径注册并指定顺序。配置完成后确认该中间件是否还需要通过其他专用设置启用。

## Objective

正确注册并排序 Spider 中间件以控制处理链行为
## Applicable Signals

- 需要启用自定义 Spider 中间件
- 需要禁用或替换内置中间件

## Contraindications

- 中间件还需额外专用设置才能生效而未确认

## Intervention Moves

- 在 SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES 字典中添加中间件类路径与顺序值
- 将内置中间件值设为 None 以禁用
- 以新类路径注册替换中间件并指定顺序

## Workflow Steps

- 确定要启用、禁用或替换的中间件类路径
- 在 SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES 字典中为每个中间件指定类路径与顺序值
- 如需禁用内置中间件，将其值设为 None
- 如需替换内置中间件，先禁用原中间件再注册新中间件并指定顺序
- 确认该中间件是否还需通过其他专用设置启用

## Constraints

- SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES 为字典，键为中间件类路径，值为中间件顺序
- 禁用内置中间件须将值设为 None

## Cautions

- 部分中间件可能需要通过特定设置额外启用，需查阅对应中间件文档确认

## Output Contract

- SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES 配置字典，含类路径与顺序值

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 启用自定义 Spider 中间件
- Therapist/Output: SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES = {
    "myproject.middlewares.CustomSpiderMiddleware": 543,
}

### Example 2

- Client/Input: 禁用内置 RefererMiddleware 并替换为自定义中间件
- Therapist/Output: SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES = {
    "scrapy.spidermiddlewares.referer.RefererMiddleware": None,
    "myproject.middlewares.CustomRefererSpiderMiddleware": 700,
}

skill_specs.name: 编写自定义 Spider 中间件钩子方法
skill_specs.description: 实现 SpiderMiddleware 子类的钩子方法（process_start、process_start_requests、process_spider_input），用于定制 Spider 启动输出、进入 Spider 的响应以及 Spider 产出的请求与 item 的处理逻辑。
skill_specs.skill_body:
实现一个 SpiderMiddleware 子类，按需覆盖一个或多个钩子方法：
1. 继承 scrapy.spidermiddlewares.SpiderMiddleware。
2. 若需处理 Spider 启动输出，实现 async process_start(start)，遍历 start 并 yield 与 start 相同类型的对象；如需兼容 2.13 以下版本，另实现同步 process_start_requests(start, spider) 并 yield from start。
3. 若需处理进入 Spider 的响应，实现 process_spider_input(response)，返回 None 表示继续处理，或抛出异常中断。
4. 仅实现当前需求所需的钩子，保持方法职责单一。
5. 完成后交由注册配置环节将类路径写入 SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES。

## Objective

实现一个或多个 Spider 中间件钩子方法以定制处理流程
## Applicable Signals

- 需要拦截并处理发往 Spider 的响应
- 需要处理 Spider 生成的请求或 item
- 需要定制 Spider 启动输出

## Contraindications

- 仅需调整已有中间件顺序而无需新逻辑

## Intervention Moves

- 继承 SpiderMiddleware 基类
- 实现 async process_start 遍历并 yield 启动输出
- 为旧版本补充同步 process_start_requests
- 实现 process_spider_input 返回 None 或抛出异常

## Workflow Steps

- 确认需要定制的处理点（启动输出、进入响应、产出请求/item）
- 创建继承 SpiderMiddleware 的子类
- 按需实现对应钩子方法
- 确保 process_spider_input 返回 None 或抛出异常
- 将类路径交由注册配置环节写入 SPIDER_MIDDLEWARES

## Constraints

- process_spider_input 只能返回 None 或抛出异常
- process_start 需为 async 并 yield 与 start 相同类型的对象
- 兼容旧版本时需额外提供同步 process_start_requests

## Cautions

- 部分中间件可能还需通过特定设置启用，需查阅对应中间件文档

## Output Contract

- 可注册的 SpiderMiddleware 子类，含已实现的钩子方法

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 需要处理 Spider 启动输出
- Therapist/Output: async def process_start(self, start):
    async for item_or_request in start:
        yield item_or_request
- Notes: 兼容旧版本可另加同步 process_start_requests

### Example 2

- Client/Input: 需要处理进入 Spider 的响应
- Therapist/Output: 实现 process_spider_input(response)，返回 None 继续处理或抛出异常中断

skill_specs.name: process_spider_input 返回值契约
skill_specs.description: 确保自定义 Spider 中间件的 process_spider_input 钩子符合 Scrapy 框架契约：对每个进入 Spider 的响应调用，必须返回 None 或抛出异常；返回 None 时处理链继续执行后续中间件直至交给 Spider。用于实现该钩子时校验返回值行为。
skill_specs.skill_body:
实现或审查 process_spider_input 方法时，确认其返回值符合契约：正常放行时返回 None，让 Scrapy 继续执行后续中间件直至响应交给 Spider；需要中断或报错时抛出异常。不要返回其他值，也不要在该方法内直接处理响应内容。

## Objective

保证 process_spider_input 返回值符合框架约定
## Applicable Signals

- 正在编写 process_spider_input 方法
- 需要确认响应是否继续沿中间件链传递

## Contraindications

- 实现其他不涉及该返回契约的钩子

## Intervention Moves

- 正常放行时返回 None
- 需要中断时抛出异常
- 避免返回其他值

## Workflow Steps

- 确认当前实现的是 process_spider_input 钩子
- 在正常路径返回 None 以继续处理链
- 在需要中断或报错时抛出异常
- 检查方法中不存在返回非 None 值的分支

## Constraints

- 返回值只能是 None 或抛出异常
- 返回 None 后由 Scrapy 继续执行后续中间件直至交给 Spider

## Cautions

- 不要在该钩子中返回响应对象或其他值来替代框架的继续处理逻辑

## Output Contract

- 返回 None 或抛出异常的实现，处理链可继续

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 实现 process_spider_input 以放行响应
- Therapist/Output: def process_spider_input(self, response):

skill_specs.name: Spider输出处理钩子实现
skill_specs.description: 实现 process_spider_output(response, result) 钩子，对 Spider 处理响应后返回的 Request/item 可迭代结果进行拦截与改写，并返回新的可迭代对象。适用于需要在爬虫输出进入后续中间件前统一过滤或转换结果的场景。
skill_specs.skill_body:
实现 process_spider_output(response, result) 钩子：接收当前 response 与 Spider 返回的 result（Request 与 item 对象的可迭代对象），对结果流进行过滤或改写，并返回一个由 Request 对象和 item 对象组成的可迭代对象。确保返回值符合契约，供后续 Spider 中间件继续处理。

## Objective

在 Spider 输出阶段拦截并改写 Request/item 结果流
## Applicable Signals

- Spider 已处理响应并返回结果流
- 需要在结果流进入后续中间件前介入

## Contraindications

- 处理的是下载器请求/响应阶段而非 Spider 输出
- 仅需记录日志而无需改变结果流

## Intervention Moves

- 定义 process_spider_output(response, result) 方法
- 遍历 result 中的 Request 与 item 对象
- 按需过滤或转换结果
- 返回新的 Request/item 可迭代对象

## Workflow Steps

- 实现 process_spider_output(response, result) 方法，接收 response 与 Spider 返回的 result
- 对 result 中的 Request 对象和 item 对象进行过滤或改写
- 返回由 Request 对象和 item 对象组成的可迭代对象

## Constraints

- process_spider_output 必须返回 Request 对象和 item 对象的可迭代对象
- response 为生成该输出的响应对象
- result 为 Spider 返回的可迭代结果

## Cautions

- 若 result 为异步可迭代对象，需改用 process_spider_output_async 异步生成器变体
- 异常处理应使用 process_spider_exception，而非在输出钩子中吞掉异常

## Output Contract

- 返回符合契约的 Request/item 可迭代对象

skill_specs.name: Spider中间件异步输出钩子实现
skill_specs.description: 实现 process_spider_output_async 异步生成器方法，在 Spider 输出结果为异步可迭代对象时替代同步 process_spider_output 被调用，用于异步爬虫管道中处理异步结果流。
skill_specs.skill_body:
在 Spider 中间件中定义 async 生成器方法 process_spider_output_async(response, result)。当 Spider 返回的 result 为异步可迭代对象时，Scrapy 会调用该方法而非 process_spider_output。方法需以异步生成器形式产出 Request 对象与 item 对象，保持与同步输出钩子一致的输出语义。

## Objective

在异步结果流场景下提供异步输出处理
## Applicable Signals

- Spider 输出结果为异步可迭代对象
- 需要异步生成器形式的输出处理

## Contraindications

- 结果为同步可迭代对象
- 未启用异步爬虫管道

## Intervention Moves

- 定义 async 生成器方法 process_spider_output_async(response, result)
- 在方法内异步产出 Request 对象与 item 对象
- 确保仅在 result 为异步可迭代时依赖该钩子

## Workflow Steps

- 确认 Spider 输出 result 为异步可迭代对象
- 在中间件中定义 async 生成器方法 process_spider_output_async(response, result)
- 在生成器中产出 Request 对象与 item 对象
- 验证异步结果流被正确传递至后续中间件

## Constraints

- 方法必须为异步生成器
- 仅在 result 为异步可迭代对象时被调用，替代 process_spider_output

## Cautions

- 同步结果流仍走 process_spider_output，不应依赖异步钩子处理

## Output Contract

- 定义可被调用的异步生成器方法 process_spider_output_async，产出 Request 与 item 对象

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: Spider 返回异步可迭代的 result
- Therapist/Output: process_spider_output_async(response, result) 作为异步生成器被调用并产出 Request 与 item
- Notes: 仅在 result 为异步可迭代时触发

skill_specs.name: Spider 中间件异常处理钩子实现
skill_specs.description: 实现 process_spider_exception 钩子，在 Spider 或上游 process_spider_output 抛异常时，决定返回 None 让异常继续传播，或返回 Request/item 可迭代对象接管输出管道。
skill_specs.skill_body:
在自定义 Spider 中间件中实现 process_spider_exception(response, exception) 钩子。判断当前异常是否应由本中间件接管：若需继续传播，返回 None，Scrapy 会继续调用后续中间件的 process_spider_exception，直至异常到达引擎被记录并丢弃；若需接管，返回一个 Request 或 item 对象的可迭代对象，此时 process_spider_output 管道从下一个中间件开始执行，且不再调用其他 process_spider_exception。确保返回值类型符合契约，不要返回非可迭代的单个对象。

## Objective

在 Spider 阶段异常时选择继续传播或接管输出
## Applicable Signals

- Spider 或上游 process_spider_output 抛出异常
- 需要自定义异常走向而非默认记录丢弃
- 需要在异常后恢复 Request/item 输出流

## Contraindications

- 处理正常输出流而非异常时应使用 process_spider_output
- 异常应直接交由引擎记录丢弃时无需实现该钩子

## Intervention Moves

- 实现 process_spider_exception(response, exception) 方法
- 判断异常是否由本中间件接管
- 返回 None 表示继续传播
- 返回 Request/item 可迭代对象表示接管并进入 process_spider_output 管道

## Workflow Steps

- 定义 process_spider_exception(response, exception) 方法
- 根据 response 与 exception 判断是否接管
- 若继续传播则返回 None
- 若接管则返回 Request 或 item 对象的可迭代对象
- 确认接管后 process_spider_output 从下一个中间件开始执行且不再调用其他 process_spider_exception

## Constraints

- 返回值只能是 None 或 Request/item 的可迭代对象
- 返回 None 时异常继续沿中间件链传播至引擎
- 返回可迭代对象时不再调用其他 process_spider_exception

## Cautions

- 返回非可迭代的单个对象会违反返回契约
- 接管异常会跳过后续中间件的异常处理钩子

## Output Contract

- 返回 None 或 Request/item 可迭代对象以明确异常走向

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: Spider 处理响应时抛出异常，本中间件希望让引擎记录丢弃
- Therapist/Output: process_spider_exception 返回 None
- Notes: 异常继续传播至引擎

### Example 2

- Client/Input: Spider 处理响应时抛出异常，本中间件希望恢复输出流
- Therapist/Output: process_spider_exception 返回包含 Request 或 item 的可迭代对象
- Notes: process_spider_output 从下一个中间件开始执行

skill_specs.name: 自定义Spider中间件基类实现
skill_specs.description: 使用BaseSpiderMiddleware基类简化异步process_spider_output()和process_start()方法的实现，通过get_processed_item/get_processed_request逐项处理spider输出，减少样板代码。
skill_specs.skill_body:
当需要编写包含异步process_spider_output()或process_start()方法的spider中间件时，继承scrapy.spidermiddlewares.base.BaseSpiderMiddleware，并实现get_processed_item(item, response)与/或get_processed_request(request, response)辅助方法。对每个来自start seeds或spider输出的item/request逐项处理：返回相同或不同的对象，或返回None以忽略该项。response参数在start seeds场景下为None。若中间件不包含这两个方法，则无需使用该基类。

## Objective

用基类辅助方法减少自定义spider中间件的样板代码并正确逐项处理item/request
## Applicable Signals

- 中间件需实现异步process_spider_output或process_start
- 存在大量重复的逐项处理样板代码

## Contraindications

- 中间件不包含process_spider_output或process_start方法
- 仅需同步简单钩子

## Intervention Moves

- 继承BaseSpiderMiddleware基类
- 实现get_processed_item逐项处理item
- 实现get_processed_request逐项处理request
- 对需忽略的项返回None

## Workflow Steps

- 确认中间件包含process_spider_output或process_start方法
- 继承scrapy.spidermiddlewares.base.BaseSpiderMiddleware
- 实现get_processed_item(item, response)返回处理后item或None
- 实现get_processed_request(request, response)返回处理后request或None
- 在start seeds场景下将response视为None

## Constraints

- 仅当中间件包含process_spider_output或process_start时才使用该基类
- 辅助方法必须逐项处理并返回相同/不同对象或None

## Cautions

- start seeds场景下response为None，需处理该情况

## Output Contract

- 可运行的spider中间件类，正确返回处理后的item/request或None以忽略

## Example Therapist Responses

- Client/Input: 需要编写异步process_spider_output的中间件
- Therapist/Output: 继承BaseSpiderMiddleware并实现get_processed_item，对每个item返回处理后对象或None
- Notes: response在start seeds时为None

skill_specs.name: Spider输出逐项过滤与改写
skill_specs.description: 对spider输出或start seeds中的单个item/request进行逐项处理：保留原样、改写为不同对象，或返回None丢弃，从而实现输出过滤与转换。
skill_specs.skill_body:
当需要过滤或改写spider产出的item，或需要拦截/替换request时，使用本技能。对每个item或request单独做决策：返回同一对象表示保留，返回不同对象表示改写，返回None表示忽略该项。处理item时调用get_processed_item(item, response)，处理request时调用对应的request处理方法；response为None表示该项来自start seeds。

## Objective

逐项决定item/request的保留、改写或丢弃
## Applicable Signals

- spider输出中存在需要过滤的item
- spider输出中存在需要拦截或替换的request
- start seeds中的item/request需要逐项处理

## Contraindications

- 无需对spider输出做任何变更时不应使用

## Intervention Moves

- 对单个item调用get_processed_item(item, response)
- 对单个request调用对应的request处理方法
- 返回同一对象以保留
- 返回不同对象以改写
- 返回None以忽略该项

- 接收来自spider输出或start seeds的单个item/request
- 判断该项应保留、改写还是丢弃

- 对每个item/request重复上述逐项决策

## Constraints

- 每次只处理单个item或request
- response为None表示该项来自start seeds
- 返回值必须是item/request对象或None

## Cautions

- 改写时应返回新的有效对象，避免返回无效类型
- 返回None会静默丢弃该项，需确认丢弃符合预期

## Output Contract

- 返回相同或不同的item/request，或返回None表示忽略该项

skill_specs.name: Offsite请求域名过滤
skill_specs.description: 在请求被调度时，基于spider允许域名的正则判断请求是否属于站内；站外请求应被忽略，站内请求继续进入调度。用于控制爬虫只跟随允许域名范围内的链接。
skill_specs.skill_body:
当请求进入调度阶段时，使用spider允许域名正则对请求hostname进行匹配：解析请求URL得到hostname（无法解析时视为空字符串），用host_regex.search(host)判断是否站内；站内请求放行继续调度，站外请求按忽略处理。

## Objective

在请求调度阶段过滤掉不属于允许域名的站外请求
## Applicable Signals

- spider已配置允许域名范围
- 请求被调度时需判断是否站内
- 存在站外链接需要被拦截

## Contraindications

- 需要跨域抓取且无域名白名单
- 请求URL无法解析出hostname时不应直接放行

## Intervention Moves

- 在spider_opened时构建host_regex
- 在request_scheduled中调用process_request处理请求
- 用urlparse_cached获取hostname，None时置为空字符串
- 用host_regex.search(host)判断是否站内并决定放行或忽略

## Workflow Steps

- spider_opened阶段通过get_host_regex(spider)构建host_regex
- 请求被调度时触发request_scheduled，调用process_request
- 解析请求得到hostname，无法解析时使用空字符串
- 用host_regex.search(host)判断是否站内
- 站内请求继续进入调度，站外请求被忽略

## Constraints

- 域名判断必须基于spider允许域名正则
- hostname为None时不得直接放行，应按空字符串处理

## Cautions

- hostname可能为None（如javascript链接），需按空字符串处理以避免误判
- 过滤发生在调度阶段，需确保host_regex在spider_opened时已构建

## Output Contract

- 站外请求被忽略，站内请求继续进入调度

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 请求hostname不在允许域名正则范围内
- Therapist/Output: 该请求被忽略，不进入调度
- Notes: 站外请求拦截

### Example 2

- Client/Input: 请求hostname匹配允许域名正则
- Therapist/Output: 该请求继续进入调度
- Notes: 站内请求放行

skill_specs.description: 在 spider_opened 阶段根据 spider 配置构建用于匹配允许域名的 host_regex 正则对象，供后续请求过滤逻辑复用。
skill_specs.skill_body:
在 spider_opened 阶段调用 get_host_regex(spider) 构建 host_regex 正则对象并保存为实例属性，供后续 should_follow 等请求过滤逻辑复用。仅做规则初始化，不在此步骤过滤请求。

- spider启动时需要初始化域名匹配规则

## Contraindications

## Intervention Moves

- 在spider_opened中调用get_host_regex(spider)
- 将返回的正则对象保存为self.host_regex供后续复用

- 在spider_opened(self, spider)中调用self.get_host_regex(spider)

- 后续请求过滤逻辑直接复用该正则对象

## Cautions

- hostname可能为None（如javascript链接），匹配时需容错处理

## Output Contract

- 生成可复用的host_regex正则对象

skill_specs.name: 请求hostname安全判定
skill_specs.description: 对单个请求解析其URL的hostname，并用已初始化的允许域名正则判断该请求是否应被跟随；hostname为空（如javascript链接等错误URL）时按不匹配处理。用于单请求的站内/站外判定。
skill_specs.skill_body:
输入一个请求对象与已初始化的host_regex。先通过缓存的URL解析取得请求的hostname；若hostname为None或空字符串，则视为不匹配。否则用host_regex对hostname执行search，返回布尔结果表示是否应跟随该请求。不要在此步骤构建或修改正则，也不要执行调度阶段的过滤逻辑。

## Objective

判断单个请求是否属于允许域名
## Applicable Signals

- 需要对单个请求做站内/站外判定
- host_regex已初始化可用

## Contraindications

- host_regex尚未初始化
- 需要构建或修改允许域名正则
- 需要执行调度阶段的批量过滤

## Intervention Moves

- 用缓存URL解析获取请求hostname
- hostname为空时按不匹配处理
- 用host_regex对hostname执行search并返回布尔结果

## Workflow Steps

- 取得已初始化的host_regex
- 通过urlparse_cached解析请求，取hostname，空值置为空字符串
- 用host_regex.search(host)判断是否匹配
- 返回布尔值表示是否应跟随该请求

## Constraints

- hostname可能为None（如javascript链接），须按不匹配处理
- 仅做单请求判定，不构建正则、不做调度过滤

## Cautions

- host_regex未初始化时不应调用本判定

## Output Contract

- 返回布尔值表示是否应跟随该请求

skill_specs.name: 下载器中间件激活与排序配置
skill_specs.description: 通过 DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES 设置注册自定义下载器中间件并指定执行顺序，可用 None 禁用内置中间件。适用于需要全局改变请求/响应处理链的场景。
skill_specs.skill_body:
在 Scrapy 项目的 settings 中配置 DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES 字典：键为中间件类路径，值为中间件顺序（整数）。如需禁用某个内置中间件，将其类路径的值设为 None。配置完成后确认中间件依赖的专属设置是否已启用。

## Objective

正确注册并排序下载器中间件，使请求/响应处理链按预期生效
## Applicable Signals

- 需要启用自定义下载器中间件
- 需要调整或禁用内置中间件顺序

## Contraindications

- 仅需修改爬虫解析逻辑而非请求/响应链
- 中间件依赖的专属设置尚未确认

## Intervention Moves

- 在 DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES 中添加中间件类路径与顺序值
- 将需禁用的内置中间件类路径值设为 None
- 确认中间件依赖的专属设置已启用

## Workflow Steps

- 确定要启用的自定义下载器中间件类路径
- 在 DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES 字典中为每个中间件指定顺序值
- 如需禁用内置中间件，将其类路径值设为 None
- 检查中间件是否依赖特定设置并确认已启用

## Constraints

- DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES 为字典，键为中间件类路径，值为中间件顺序
- 禁用内置中间件时使用 None 作为值

## Cautions

- 部分中间件可能需要通过特定设置启用，需查阅各中间件文档

## Output Contract

- DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES 配置字典，含类路径与顺序值

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 需要启用自定义下载器中间件
- Therapist/Output: DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES = {
    "myproject.middlewares.CustomDownloaderMiddleware": 543,
}

### Example 2

- Client/Input: 需要禁用内置 UserAgentMiddleware
- Therapist/Output: DOWNLOADER_MIDDLEWARES = {
    "myproject.middlewares.CustomDownloaderMiddleware": 543,
    "scrapy.downloadermiddlewares.useragent.UserAgentMiddleware": None,
}

skill_specs.name: Scrapy 请求构造与回调数据传递
skill_specs.description: 构造 scrapy.Request 时正确设置 url、callback、errback、cb_kwargs、cookies、priority、dont_filter 等参数，并把附加数据通过 cb_kwargs 传给回调。适用于需要发起请求并向下游回调传递上下文数据的场景。
skill_specs.skill_body:
在需要发起新的抓取请求时，构造 scrapy.Request 对象：明确设置 url；按需绑定 callback 与 errback；将需要传给回调的上下文数据放入 cb_kwargs（dict，会作为关键字参数传给 callback）；如需设置 cookie，使用 Request 的 cookies 参数而非 Cookie 头；按需设置 priority、dont_filter、encoding、flags 等参数。构造完成后确认回调与 cb_kwargs 已正确绑定。

## Objective

构造可正确路由回调并携带附加数据的 Scrapy 请求
## Applicable Signals

- 需要发起新的抓取请求
- 需要向回调函数传递额外上下文数据

## Contraindications

- 仅需解析已有响应
- 需要设置 Cookie 头而非 cookies 参数

## Intervention Moves

- 设置 url 参数
- 绑定 callback 与 errback
- 通过 cb_kwargs 传递附加数据给回调
- 使用 cookies 参数设置请求 cookie
- 按需设置 priority、dont_filter、encoding、flags

## Workflow Steps

- 确定请求目标 url
- 按需绑定 callback 与 errback
- 将需要传给回调的上下文数据放入 cb_kwargs
- 如需 cookie，使用 Request 的 cookies 参数而非 Cookie 头
- 按需设置 priority、dont_filter、encoding、flags 等参数
- 确认回调与 cb_kwargs 已正确绑定

## Constraints

- cb_kwargs 必须是 dict，会作为关键字参数传给 callback
- 设置 cookie 应使用 Request.cookies 参数，通过 Cookie 头设置的 cookie 不被 CookiesMiddleware 处理

## Cautions

- 通过 Cookie 头设置的 cookie 不被 CookiesMiddleware 考虑，这是已知限制

## Output Contract

- 一个配置完整、回调与 cb_kwargs 正确绑定的 Request 对象

skill_specs.name: Scrapy 请求 errback 失败处理
skill_specs.description: 为 Scrapy 请求设置 errback 回调，在请求处理失败时接收 Failure 对象并执行降级、重试或记录；适用于需要容错处理的抓取请求。
skill_specs.skill_body:
当请求可能失败且需要容错时，在构造 Request 时通过 errback 参数指定回调函数。errback 接收 Failure 对象，可在其中读取请求附加数据（如 cb_kwargs 或 meta）以完成降级、重试或记录。仅处理失败路径，不替代成功回调。

## Objective

在请求失败时通过 errback 捕获并处理异常
## Applicable Signals

- 请求可能失败需要容错
- 需要在失败时读取请求附加数据

## Contraindications

- 请求无需失败处理
- 仅处理成功响应

## Intervention Moves

- 在 Request 构造时设置 errback 参数指向处理函数
- errback 函数接收 Failure 对象并据此执行降级或记录
- 在 errback 中访问请求附加数据（cb_kwargs 或 meta）

## Workflow Steps

- 判断该请求是否需要失败容错处理
- 构造 Request 时通过 errback 参数指定失败处理函数
- 在 errback 函数中接收 Failure 对象
- 根据 Failure 与请求附加数据执行降级、重试或记录

## Constraints

- errback 默认值为 None，需显式设置才会触发失败处理
- errback 仅处理失败路径，成功响应仍由 callback 处理

## Cautions

- 通过 Cookie 头设置的 cookie 不被 CookiesMiddleware 识别，如需设置 cookie 应使用 Request.cookies 参数

## Output Contract

- errback 函数接收 Failure 并完成降级或记录

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 构造一个可能失败的请求并需要失败时记录
- Therapist/Output: 在 Request 中设置 errback 指向处理函数，函数接收 Failure 并记录失败信息
- Notes: errback 默认 None，需显式指定

skill_specs.name: Scrapy Request 回调与错误回调路由配置
skill_specs.description: 为 Scrapy Request 指定 callback 或 errback，并处理 None/NO_CALLBACK 默认行为，使响应或异常被路由到正确的处理函数。适用于需要自定义响应处理或捕获请求处理异常的场景。
skill_specs.skill_body:
在构造 Scrapy Request 时，明确指定 callback 用于处理正常响应、errback 用于处理异常。若 callback 为 None（默认），则响应交由 spider 的 parse() 方法处理；若使用 NO_CALLBACK()，则显式声明不回调。注意 HttpErrorMiddleware 默认对非 2xx 响应抛出异常并转交 errback，因此需要捕获 HTTP 错误时应配置 errback。

## Objective

正确配置请求的回调与错误回调路由
## Applicable Signals

- 需要自定义响应处理函数
- 需要捕获请求处理异常
- 需要显式声明不回调

## Contraindications

- 使用默认 parse 即可满足需求

## Intervention Moves

- 为 Request 指定 callback 处理正常响应
- 为 Request 指定 errback 处理异常
- 使用 None 默认交由 parse() 处理
- 使用 NO_CALLBACK() 显式声明不回调

## Workflow Steps

- 判断是否需要自定义响应处理：若默认 parse() 足够，则 callback 保持 None。
- 若需自定义处理，指定 callback 为对应处理函数。
- 若需捕获请求处理异常，指定 errback 为异常处理函数。
- 若需显式声明不回调，使用 NO_CALLBACK()。
- 注意 HttpErrorMiddleware 默认对非 2xx 响应抛出异常并转交 errback，据此配置错误处理。

## Constraints

- callback 为 None 时响应交由 spider 的 parse() 方法处理
- NO_CALLBACK() 用于显式声明不回调

## Cautions

- HttpErrorMiddleware 默认对非 2xx 响应抛出异常并发送到 errback，未配置 errback 时异常可能未被捕获

## Output Contract

- Request 携带正确的 callback/errback 配置

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 需要自定义响应处理函数
- Therapist/Output: Request(url, callback=self.custom_parse)

### Example 2

- Client/Input: 需要捕获请求处理异常
- Therapist/Output: Request(url, callback=self.parse, errback=self.handle_error)

skill_specs.name: Scrapy Request 复制与替换
skill_specs.description: 使用 Request.copy() 或 Request.replace() 基于现有请求派生新请求，仅覆盖指定字段，并默认浅拷贝 cb_kwargs 与 meta。适用于需要在保留原请求上下文的前提下修改 URL、回调、优先级等字段时。
skill_specs.skill_body:
当需要基于已有 Request 派生新请求时：1) 若只需原样复制，调用 copy()；2) 若需修改部分字段，调用 replace() 并仅传入要覆盖的关键字参数（如 url、callback、priority、dont_filter 等）；3) 注意 cb_kwargs 与 meta 默认被浅拷贝，若需修改嵌套结构须显式传入新值或自行深拷贝；4) 确认返回的新 Request 除指定字段外其余属性与原请求一致。

## Objective

在保留原请求属性的基础上安全派生修改后的请求对象
## Applicable Signals

- 已有 Request 对象可作为派生基础
- 仅需覆盖 url、callback、priority、dont_filter 等少量字段
- 需要保留原请求的 meta 或 cb_kwargs 上下文

## Contraindications

- 需要完全新建无关请求
- 需要深拷贝嵌套 meta 结构时未显式处理

## Intervention Moves

- 调用 Request.copy() 获得原样副本
- 调用 Request.replace() 并仅传入需覆盖的关键字参数
- 对需要修改的嵌套 meta 或 cb_kwargs 显式传入新值或自行深拷贝

## Workflow Steps

- 确认存在可作为基础的现有 Request 对象
- 判断是原样复制（copy）还是字段覆盖（replace）
- 使用 replace() 时仅传入需修改的字段，其余保持默认
- 检查 cb_kwargs 与 meta 的浅拷贝语义，必要时显式处理嵌套结构
- 验证返回的新 Request 除指定字段外与原请求一致

## Constraints

- replace() 的 cb_kwargs 与 meta 默认浅拷贝，除非显式传入新值
- 仅覆盖明确指定的字段，不应意外改变其它属性

## Cautions

- 浅拷贝可能导致嵌套结构共享引用，修改嵌套内容时需谨慎

## Output Contract

- 返回一个仅指定字段被覆盖、其余属性与原请求一致的新 Request 对象

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 已有 Request 对象，需要将其 priority 提高并更换 callback
- Therapist/Output: request.replace(priority=10, callback=new_callback)
- Notes: 其余字段及 meta、cb_kwargs 默认浅拷贝保留

### Example 2

- Client/Input: 需要原样复制一个 Request 对象
- Therapist/Output: request.copy()
- Notes: 返回该请求的副本
